name: Mafia
description: One day n friends gathered together to play "Mafia". During each round of the game some player must be the supervisor and other n - 1 people take part in the game. For each person we know in how many rounds he wants to be a player, not the supervisor: the i -th person wants to play a i rounds. What is the minimum number of rounds of the "Mafia" game they need to play to let each person play at least as many rounds as they want?
input_specification: The first line contains integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) . The second line contains n space-separated integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ) — the i -th number in the list is the number of rounds the i -th person wants to play.
output_specification: In a single line print a single integer — the minimum number of game rounds the friends need to let the i -th person play at least a i rounds. Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin , cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 348A — Mafia [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
